en: And it centers around Valentine's Day and a simulation that happened as a result.

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you explain what happened and how that potentially led to the early days of Simile?

speaker: Unknown
en: So this was 2023.
zh: 那是在 2023 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had this idea that large language models are often used for simple tasks like classification, simple generation.
zh: 我们有一个想法，就是大型语言模型通常被用于简单的任务，比如分类、简单的生成。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we thought that these models actually had a lot more potential.
zh: 但我们认为这些模型实际上有更多的潜力。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the early observations that we made was that these models are trained on so much of human behavioral data, sentiment data that were expressed on the web.
zh: 我们早期的观察之一是，这些模型是在大量的人类行为数据、在网络上表达的情感数据上训练的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you poke at them sort of at the right angle, you could actually extract a lot of realistic human behaviors out of them.
zh: 所以如果你以正确的角度去刺激它们，你实际上可以从它们中提取出很多真实的人类行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought that was really interesting.
zh: 我认为这非常有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was also particularly interesting in that it was domain agnostic.
zh: 这一点特别有趣，因为它是领域无关的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you look at the literature in computer science, for many decades, we've always had the vision of creating agents that are meant to be generalizable, that are meant to really be able to act like human in any environment.
zh: 所以如果你看计算机科学的文献，几十年来，我们一直有一个愿景，就是创建旨在可泛化的智能体，旨在能够在任何环境中真正像人类一样行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my mind went to, well, maybe we have that opportunity here.
zh: 我的想法是，好吧，也许我们在这里有机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what we ended up doing was, well, if we were to fast forward many years into doing this, what would be the most ambitious vision that we might have?
zh: 所以我们最终做的是，好吧，如果我们快进很多年来做这件事，我们可能拥有的最雄心勃勃的愿景是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was creating an entire lived experience of a town.
zh: 那就是创造一个城镇的完整生活体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the idea here was we would make a game town, and we would populate it with 25 NPCs, so non-playable characters, except these characters would actually wake up in the morning, do their routines, go to work, have relationships, and do all that.
zh: 这里的想法是我们要做一个游戏城镇，我们要在里面填充 25 个 NPC，也就是非玩家角色，除了这些角色实际上会在早上醒来，做他们的日常事务，去工作，建立关系，做所有这些事。

speaker: Unknown
en: They would actually remember their interactions.
zh: 他们实际上会记住他们的互动。

speaker: Unknown
en: They would actually plan their days.
zh: 他们实际上会计划他们的一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some of the surprising things you end up seeing was the simulation itself was set the day before Valentine's Day.
zh: 你最终会看到的一些令人惊讶的事情是，模拟本身被设定在情人节的前一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you actually see these agents come together, have parties, like self-organize.
zh: 你实际上会看到这些智能体聚在一起，举行聚会，像自我组织一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they would actually plan parties.
zh: 所以他们实际上会策划聚会。

speaker: Unknown
en: They would decorate the cafe.
zh: 他们会装饰咖啡馆。

speaker: Unknown
en: We thought that was really interesting.
zh: 我们认为这非常有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, two fundamental contributions from that work.
zh: 现在那项工作有两个基本贡献。

speaker: Unknown
en: One was it was one of the earliest examples of creating agents.
zh: 一个是它是创建智能体的最早的例子之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this particular set of agents were paired with, back in the day, GPT-3.5, TextAvanshi.
zh: 所以这一组特定的智能体在当时是与 GPT-3.5、TextAvanshi 配对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we didn't quite have ChatGPT back then.
zh: 所以那时我们还没有 ChatGPT。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it was paired with memory planning and reflection.
zh: 然后它与记忆、规划和反思配对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really the first times that those concepts came out to be an explicit part of the architecture in quote-unquote agentic workflows.
zh: 这是这些概念首次成为所谓的“智能体工作流”架构的明确部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason why we actually got that inspiration was if you had more than one agent side by side, you want them to remember each other.
zh: 我们实际上得到那个灵感的原因是，如果你有不止一个智能体并排，你希望他们记住彼此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Back in the day, language models didn't really have the concept of memory.
zh: 那时候，语言模型并没有记忆的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I thought, okay, you have to give them the memory so that they don't say, hey, nice meeting you every time they meet their roommate.
zh: 所以我想，好吧，你必须给他们记忆，这样他们就不会每次见到室友时都说，嘿，很高兴见到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we had them have this concept of memory and planning and reflection to make sense of very long-term landscape.
zh: 所以我们让他们拥有记忆、规划和反思的概念，以理解非常长期的格局。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you solve that memory problem?
zh: 你如何解决那个记忆问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because everyone says, oh, we have a memory problem today.
zh: 因为每个人都说，哦，我们今天有一个记忆问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you solve the memory problem of agents to prevent that from happening?
zh: 你如何解决智能体的记忆问题以防止这种情况发生？

speaker: Unknown
en: So back in the day, it was actually, the initial idea was fairly simple.
zh: 所以在过去，实际上，最初的想法相当简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: These language models are actually quite good at parsing natural language, so we put everything in markdown text file.
zh: 这些语言模型实际上非常擅长解析自然语言，所以我们把所有东西都放在 markdown 文本文件里。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was it.
zh: 就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: That sort of worked.
zh: 那种方法行得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the issue there, however, is because the language models have context window, and even today, even if the context window is getting larger, the kind of experiences that these agents can have in the small game town is immense.
zh: 然而，现在的问题是，因为语言模型有上下文窗口，而且即使在今天，即使上下文窗口变得越来越大，这些智能体在小镇游戏中可能拥有的体验种类也是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And imagine now if we were to bring this to real life in a world like the one we live in, the amount of memory that we accumulate is huge.
zh: 现在想象一下，如果我们把它带到现实生活中，在我们生活的这样一个世界里，我们积累的记忆量是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the problem becomes, how do you make sense of this large quantity of memory?
zh: 所以问题变成了，你如何理解这大量的记忆？

speaker: Unknown
en: So imagine you went to get omelet five times in a day.
zh: 所以想象一下你一天中去取了五次蛋卷。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to make sense of that aside from, oh, I went to get omelet five times throughout the week or something like that.
zh: 你想理解这一点，而不是，噢，我这周取了五次蛋卷之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we had this concept of reflection, which basically was every certain interval, it's like a shower thought, you ask agent explicitly to get bunch of their memory pieces and basically make sense of them.
zh: 所以我们有这个反思的概念，基本上是每隔一定的时间间隔，就像淋浴时的想法一样，你明确地要求智能体获取一堆他们的记忆片段，并基本上理解它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did you get omelet so often this week?
zh: 你这周为什么这么频繁地吃蛋卷？

speaker: Unknown
en: Were you busy?
zh: 你很忙吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you like omelet?
zh: 你喜欢蛋卷吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why are you studying for this test so hard?
zh: 你为什么如此努力地学习这项考试？

speaker: Unknown
en: You are in library every single day.
zh: 你每天都在图书馆。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does this matter to you?
zh: 这对你来说重要吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they will actually start formulating ideas that are more higher level than what happens on the ground truth.
zh: 他们实际上会开始形成比地面现实更高层次的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So gradually, they start to realize, oh, this particular research topic, I'm actually quite invested in it.
zh: 所以逐渐地，他们开始意识到，噢，这个特定的研究课题，我实际上非常投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: This might actually have something to do with my childhood or my fundamental memory.
zh: 这实际上可能和我的童年或我的基础记忆有关。

speaker: Unknown
en: This actually shapes who they are as a person.
zh: 这实际上塑造了他们作为一个人是谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that ends up becoming a very useful function in creating these agents that have personality, that actually has a point of view on the world, that can actually make sense of a lot of this data.
zh: 所以这最终成为了一个非常有用的功能，用于创造这些有个性、对世界有观点、并且能够理解大量数据的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's how we did it back in the day.
zh: 所以这就是我们过去做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when we think about a simulation model today, for those that don't know, a simulation model is essentially that.
